text:
mia: ran a focused nsys capture on fused-attn path during a 32-token generation. seeing repeated 15-30ms spikes attributed to kv write kernels when batch > 12. attaching raw timeline shortly.

sam: can you paste the nsys command you used? also did you enable nvtx ranges?

mia: yep command was: `nsys profile -o /tmp/run --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --capture-range=cudaApiCalls ./run_inference.sh`

mia: nvtx shows big yellow ranges labeled `KV_WRITE_CHUNK` and `fused_flash_attn_fw` interleaving. the write kernels are -> `cudaMemcpyAsync` to device followed by `kv_write_kernel_v2`.

oliver: interesting. is the kernel selector maybe choosing the non-streaming write variant for some sequences? we recently tightened batch threshold in kernel_selector.cpp to avoid small-launch overheads. could cause bigger contiguous writes.

mia: exactly my thought. for batches 1-11 it picks streaming-writes, for >=12 picks batched-write. something like: `if (batch_size >= 12 && avg_seq >= 16) use_batched_write=true;`

rachel: did you capture per-stream timelines? if writes block the default compute stream we get stalls in attention kernels. try moving KV writes to a dedicated copy/transfer stream and use events to sync.

mia: I re-ran with explicit async stream for kv writes, and the big spikes drop from ~25ms to ~6ms, but we still see a residual 2-3ms tail on `fused_flash_attn_fw`.

sam: can you paste condensed perf counters? sample from nvprof: 
```
Kernel, Time(ms), Calls
fused_flash_attn_fw, 3.2, 1024
kv_write_kernel_v2, 18.7, 96
memcpy_htod_async, 16.9, 96
```

oliver: that pattern screams write-amplification: each sequence triggers a full kv page write instead of incremental delta. any chance the kvcache write coalescing logic is miscomputing dirty ranges?

mia: dug into kvcache manager: coalescer uses `last_write_offset` + `chunk_size` to decide coalesce. for variable seq lengths we can overflow into next page and then fallback to full-page write. triggered by quantized layout change in `flash_variant_b` kernel.

rachel: aha — flash_variant_b changed tile layout in the last opt PR. it reduced compute for forward pass but changed byte layout for kv. kernel_selector sees incompatible layout and forces a conservative full-write path.

sam: can we short-term patch kernel_selector to recognize flash_variant_b layout and pick streaming-write? add a fast path: `if (layout == FLASH_B && gpu_arch >= sm80) use_streaming_write = true;`

mia: tested locally with that patch; end-to-end latency for batch=16 dropped ~22%. pushing gists/trace to s3: s3://redwood-infra/perf/2119998888/trace.qdrep

perf-bot: profiling artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-infra/perf/2119998888/{trace.qdrep,perf_summary.txt}. Top hotspots: [kv_write_kernel_v2, memcpy_htod_async, fused_flash_attn_fw].

oliver: nice. follow-ups: 1) small patch to kernel_selector for FLASH_B fast-path (PR), 2) add unit test that simulates mixed sequence length coalescing, 3) instrument kvcache to expose coalesce decisions via nvtx.
rachel: also recommend enabling async-kv-write by default behind a feature flag for Dedicated customers until we fully validate.

mia: opening PR now, will add perf numbers. thanks all :thumbsup:
